user_methodology_overrides: Use the 20-game 25th percentile (P25); replace the prior P16 measure.

alternate_methodology.alternate_hit_rule: Count locked L10 observations >= the alternate threshold; denominator remains 10.
alternate_methodology.core_rule: American odds inclusive -350 to -150; choose odds numerically closest to -250; ties choose more negative price.
alternate_methodology.floor_rule: Immediately lower available alternate threshold than CORE.
alternate_methodology.ceiling_rule: Immediately higher available alternate threshold than CORE.
alternate_methodology.p7_priority_rule: Flag the highest available alternate threshold strictly below the locked 20-game P7. P7 prioritization does not alter the price-target CORE rule.
alternate_methodology.p25: Retained from locked Stage 1; not recalculated.

factors.detail: Starting quarterback, full-time role; 150+ is a low threshold.
JAX averaged 242.6 pass yards and 28.0 points per game; Sharp ranks JAX pass offense 10th vs BAL pass defense 17th.
JAX is favored by roughly 9–10; Lawrence left the Week 8 blowout before the fourth quarter, creating a volume cap risk.
No Week 9 injury issue identified for Lawrence; mild temperatures and low winds expected.

context.implication: 150+ is supported by role and offense; early game control is the main risk.

factors.detail: Lead Baltimore early-down runner; likely central to the plan with a rookie QB.
JAX allows a league-low 77.4 rush yards per game and 3.4 yards per carry; NFL.com described it as the league's top run defense.
Henry has been below 60 rushing yards in each of BAL's last three losses: 53, 45 and 58; he had 11 carries for 53 at BUF.
BAL RT Roger Rosengarten and LG John Simpson were limited; JAX lost DT DaVon Hamilton for the season, which could soften the interior.
A conservative rookie-QB plan could raise carries, but BAL is a large underdog and may trail.

context.implication: 50+ is achievable but the elite run defense and recent sub-60 outputs are significant headwinds.

factors.detail: 24.6% target share (48 targets in 7 games), around 75% season snap share; Sharp reports 2.27 yards per route run.
Recent usage split shows 7.3 targets per game and 74% snaps over the last three full games.
Sharp reports BAL allowing 10.3 yards per target to WR1s (30th); JAX pass offense ranks 10th vs BAL pass defense 17th.
Meyers has hamstring/ankle issues and could be limited, but Brian Thomas Jr. and other receivers remain target competitors.
JAX is a large favorite, which may suppress late passing volume.

context.implication: 40+ is supported by target share, route efficiency and matchup; late-game volume is the key risk.
